steps.action: Place the 6x8 plate flat on the table as the base, with the long side running left to right.
watch_for: Use the 6x8 plate, not a smaller plate of similar size.

steps.action: Place the two tall slopes side by side along the back-right edge of the dark gray plate, sloped faces pointing toward the front-left.
watch_for: Slopes must face forward (sloped side toward the open plate area), not backward
Position them flush against the back edge, toward the right side of the plate

steps.action: Attach one blue 1x4 brick along the back edge to the left of the slopes, and the other along the right edge in front of the slopes.
watch_for: The two bricks go in different places: one at the back-left beside the slopes, one at the right side in front of them
Keep each brick pressed against the slopes with no gap

steps.action: Place the red 2x2 plate in the center between the blue bricks and lay the two lime tiles on either side of it, running front to back.
watch_for: Tiles go on both sides of the red plate, parallel to each other
Red plate must be centered between the two green tiles, not offset

steps.action: Add one blue 1x4 brick along the left back edge and one along the front edge of the baseplate to close in the seat.
watch_for: Front brick sits at the front edge, beside the existing right-front blue brick
Left brick continues the back row, lined up with the existing blue brick

steps.action: Stack the two red round 2x2 bricks in the center of the base, in front of the gray slopes.
watch_for: Center the round bricks over the green plate between the side walls
Push the second round brick firmly onto the first

steps.action: Place one blue 1x1 side-stud brick on top of each back corner of the side walls, next to the gray slopes, with the side studs facing outward.
watch_for: Side studs must face outward to the sides, not forward or inward
One brick goes at each back corner, left and right

steps.action: Stack the 1x2 bricks on top of the blue side walls, building up the back and front walls one layer higher around the red cylinder and gray slope.
watch_for: Stagger the bricks over the seams of the layer below so the wall stays strong
Leave the gap at the left front open as shown

steps.action: Place the two 1x1 side-stud bricks on the left ends of the back and front walls, with the side studs facing outward to the left.
watch_for: Side studs must point out to the left, not inward or forward
Place them at the left ends of the walls, not the right

steps.action: Press the finished sub-assembly into the middle of the blue body with the dark gray brick facing the front-left.
watch_for: Orient the gray brick end toward the front open side, not the gray slopes at the back.

steps.action: Place the red round 2x2 brick on the center of the red plate, toward the back between the grey slopes and the front wall.
watch_for: Center it on the red plate, not on the grey grille piece at the left
Press it fully down onto the studs

steps.action: Attach the two grey tall slopes on the left end, one at each back and front corner, with the sloped faces pointing inward toward the center.
watch_for: Slopes must face inward toward the red plate, not outward
Place them on the left end, matching the grey slopes already on the right end
Do not cover the grey grille piece between them

steps.action: Stack the four 1x4 bricks on top of the outer walls to raise the wall by one layer all around the box.
watch_for: Stagger the new bricks over the joints below so the wall stays locked together
Leave the gray sloped pieces and the side studs uncovered

steps.action: Attach the red round plate to the side stud on the left end and the gray cone to the side stud on the front face, both pointing outward.
watch_for: Use the side studs on the correct faces: red on the left end, cone on the front
Cone must point outward with its wide end against the wall

steps.action: Lay the two 1x6 plates on top of the walls, one along the back long edge and one along the front long edge, framing the open centre.
watch_for: Keep the plates flush with the outer edges of the wall so the inner opening above the red part stays clear
Align both plates on the long sides, not the short ends

steps.action: Place the two 2x4 gray plates end to end across the top, bridging the opening behind the red part to form a 2x8 strip along the long side.
watch_for: Leave the front opening over the red part uncovered
Make sure the plates span both side walls and press down on the studs at each end

steps.action: Place the two 1x6 bricks lengthwise along the back and front long edges of the top, flanking the gray plates in the middle.
watch_for: Keep the bricks on the outer long edges so the center gray plate studs stay exposed
Align ends flush with the wall below

steps.action: Attach the gray 2x2 brick onto the center gray plate, toward the back, overlapping the rear 1x6 brick edge.
watch_for: Position the brick on the correct studs at the back-left of the gray plate, not centered

steps.action: Place the four curved slopes on top in two rows of two, flanking the central gray plate, with the curves sloping down toward the front and back edges.
watch_for: Curve direction: each slope must slope away from the center toward the outer edge
Leave the central 2x2 studs exposed between the slopes

steps.action: Attach the four curved bricks at the four top corners, with the curved sides facing outward to round off the ends.
watch_for: Curves must face outward at each corner, not inward
Place them on the corner studs, not in the middle of the edge

steps.action: Place one tile along the top of each long side wall, centered between the two end studs.
watch_for: Leave the single end studs exposed at both ends of each wall
Put one tile on the front wall and one on the back wall, not both on one side

steps.action: Press one plate along the top of each long side wall, covering the tiles and the end studs.
watch_for: Align each plate flush over the full wall length so it locks onto both end studs

steps.action: Turn the model around, then place one inverted slope on each corner of the dark gray plate, with the sloped faces pointing diagonally outward.
watch_for: Rotate the model first, as the yellow turn-around icon shows
These are inverted slopes, so the slope goes underneath and faces outward, away from the plate
Each slope must sit on a corner stud and be angled diagonally outward

steps.action: Build two toast slices (1x4 plate, two staggered layers of 1x2 bricks, 1x4 plate, two slopes on top) and push them down into the toaster's two slots with the slopes facing the same side.
watch_for: Build the toast sub-assembly twice (2x)
Offset the second layer of 1x2 bricks so they overlap the joint below
Both slopes on each slice point the same way, toward the left as drawn
Rotate the model as shown by the turn-around icon before inserting

steps.action: Build two bread slices by stacking two 1x4 tan bricks and topping each with two slopes facing outward at the ends, then push the toaster lever so the brown toast pops up and set the new slices beside the toaster.
watch_for: Place the two slopes on the end studs with their sloped sides facing away from each other, leaving the middle studs exposed
Build two identical slices (2x)
Align the two stacked 1x4 bricks evenly with no overhang
